title: A Person at the Controls: The Speed They Can Drive at When They See the Past, the Dead Man's Timeout, and a Vehicle That Slows Itself for the Wall

questions.question: What does the delay of an operator add to the stopping distance?
options: The vehicle goes on at its speed for the whole delay before it starts to brake
Nothing, if the vehicle's brakes are good
A fixed 0.5 m, whatever the speed
questions.explanation: The picture is old, the person takes time, and the command takes time to arrive. All that while the vehicle keeps its speed, and only then brakes.

questions.question: The speed allowed with 0.5 s of delay in all and with 2.0 s was:
options: 4.00 m/s with either: the brakes set it
questions.explanation: For a sight line of 6 m and 2 m/s2 of braking: the more delay, the more of the 6 m is used up before braking starts.

questions.question: After the commands stopped, a vehicle at 2 m/s went on with a timeout of 0.5 s:
questions.explanation: A metre during the half second before the governor acts, and a metre of braking from 2 m/s at 2 m/s2. With a timeout of 2.0 s it was 4.99 m.

questions.question: With the obstacle sensed and the operator at full speed, the vehicle stopped:
options: At the obstacle, with nothing to spare
20 m short, where it was first sensed
questions.explanation: The governor caps the speed so the vehicle can always stop within what it senses, less a margin of 0.5 m, whatever the stick says.

questions.question: Why does the governor ramp the speed?
options: The link is too slow to carry a step
A step in the request is not a step in the wheels: it throws the load and spins them
So that the dead man's timeout has time to act
questions.explanation: The governor raises the speed no faster than the acceleration limit, so a request for 2 m/s was reached after 1.33 s.

questions.question: What does a dead man's timeout add to?
options: The margin kept from an obstacle
The stopping distance: v times the timeout
questions.explanation: Until the timeout has passed the vehicle acts on the last request. At 2 m/s, each half second of timeout is another metre.
